Find the arc length $L$ of the polar curve $r=6{e}^{3\theta }$ for $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{3}$ (shown in blue in the diagram above). Do not round the answer.

$L=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The arc length $L$ of a polar curve $r=r(\theta )$ is given by

$$
L={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r=6{e}^{3\theta },$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }=18{e}^{3\theta }.
$$

Therefore, the arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\sqrt{{(6{e}^{3\theta })}^{2}+{(18{e}^{3\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\sqrt{36{e}^{6\theta }+324{e}^{6\theta }}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\sqrt{360{e}^{6\theta }}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =6\sqrt{10}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}{e}^{3\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =6\sqrt{10}{[\frac{1}{3}{e}^{3\theta }]}_{0}^{\pi /3} \\  & =2\sqrt{10}{[{e}^{3\theta }]}_{0}^{\pi /3} \\  & =2\sqrt{10}({e}^{\pi }-{e}^{0}) \\  & =2\sqrt{10}({e}^{\pi }-1).\end{aligned}
$$
